definitions.explanation: Plants that grow naturally in fields, mountains, and roadsides without being cultivated. Includes both flowers and grasses.

examples.japanese: {道端|みちばた}に{野草|やそう}が{咲|さ}いている。
examples.english: Wild plants are blooming along the roadside.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べられる{野草|やそう}を{採|と}りに{山|やま}へ{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to the mountains to pick edible wild plants.

examples.japanese: {野草|やそう}{図鑑|ずかん}を{片手|かたて}に{散歩|さんぽ}すると、{足元|あしもと}の{植物|しょくぶつ}にも{目|め}が{行|い}くようになる。
examples.english: When you take a walk with a wild plant field guide in hand, you start noticing the plants at your feet.

notes:
A neutral term for uncultivated plants growing in the wild. Unlike {雑草|ざっそう} (weeds), which has a negative nuance of unwanted plants, {野草|やそう} is more neutral or positive, treating these plants as worthy of interest.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {野草|やそう}を{摘|つ}む (to pick wild plants)
- {食用|しょくよう}{野草|やそう} (edible wild plants)
- {野草|やそう}{図鑑|ずかん} (wild plant field guide)
- {野草|やそう}{観察|かんさつ} (wild plant observation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {野草|やそう}: wild plant (neutral/positive, nature appreciation)
- {雑草|ざっそう}: weed (unwanted plant)
- {山菜|さんさい}: wild mountain vegetables (edible, for cooking)
